mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative while GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 7% signals economic strength, boosting S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not exceed 2% when UNRATE is below 7%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production and housing starts jointly indicate economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when both proxies increase.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% monthly increase in CPI suggests inflation, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
Growth in non-farm payrolls by 50k signals economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: No increase in 5-day returns when payrolls exceed 50k.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment in a late-cycle expansion may signal inflation, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive 60-day returns in late-cycle with low unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales indicate strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative 20-day returns with rising retail sales.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate alongside high GDP indicates economic stimulus, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when both proxies indicate stimulus.
